reservoir_zhou_wen.name: Zhou Wen
reservoir_zhou_wen.title: Receiver of the basin's ordinary grain commission
reservoir_zhou_wen.appearance: Grey hair cropped at the ears, broad brown coat, ordinary scale weights and ruled account boards.
reservoir_zhou_wen.interest: Pays actual work, protects stored food and distinguishes an accurate ledger from a useful but unsupported story.

reservoir_tian_yu.name: Tian Yu
reservoir_tian_yu.title: Young clerk of the basin's grain house
reservoir_tian_yu.appearance: Untidy dark hair, quick grey eyes, ink-marked blue cuffs and a repaired wicker basket.
reservoir_tian_yu.interest: Learns accurate receiving work, trades actual shifts and enjoys jokes without confusing them with testimony.

reservoir_ep03_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_001.text: On Day One Thousand Twenty-six, Zhou Wen met Yue at the grain house's ordinary weighing bench. He had read the permitted request, not her private family letters. His first question concerned which scale and copying methods she could demonstrate without spiritual reinforcement. Yue named the ordinary work she had actually done and the parts she would need checked here. Zhou supplied a calibrated local weight and a blank receiving page. The small demonstration would occupy a paid interval inside a defined day's work if he accepted the appointment.

reservoir_ep03_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_002.text: The commission's cash had already been received: one hundred ninety copper from accepted storage charges and ten from a separately voted member contribution. Zhou counted the two hundred with the cooperative's receiver before discussing employment. None came from the contested water-turn fund or a candidate's future examination. The proposed division was public. Yue would earn forty-eight for sixteen ordinary day equivalents at three each. Seventeen other local worker-days at the same rate required fifty-one. Paper, seals and ordinary comparison materials required three more.

reservoir_ep03_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_003.text: The remaining ninety-eight purchased forty-nine accepted nights and forty-nine days of ordinary food at one copper each. Those provisions made Yue's scattered appointment workable through Day One Thousand Seventy-four. They were not cash wages and could not be transferred into an instrument order. Other workers lived locally under their own arrangements; the approved visitor provision was written separately rather than concealed in their labor line. Zhou showed the source vote and the current lodging receiver. Yue could object before accepting, and any change would need the cooperative's actual decision.

reservoir_ep03_004.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_004.text: The work schedule named sixteen days across the forty-nine-day term, leaving ordinary rest, family correspondence and weather margins. Yue's first three accepted days would fall on the twenty-sixth, thirtieth and thirty-fifth. Later work had specific dates rather than an instruction to be useful whenever anyone asked. A normal working day meant the posted hours, with meal and rest intervals shown. No new spiritual instruction belonged to this grain commission. Yue read that boundary particularly carefully while the winter-city receiving terms still had their own unfinished obligations.

reservoir_ep03_005.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_005.text: Zhou did not buy Yue's whole life by buying sixteen day equivalents. Private letters, unpaid social visits and unaccepted extra copying would remain outside the wage sheet. A changed task needed a new acceptance or an authorized substitution within the actual funded hours. She would not catch overhead loads, carry the largest sacks alone or use qi to compensate for unsuitable equipment. The work order named ordinary waist-height handling and qualified staff for heavier moves. Her shoulder limit was a practical condition of the job, not a story the receiver could admire away.

reservoir_ep03_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_006.text: The demonstration began with two ordinary weights and an empty pan. Yue checked the beam's rest position before comparing the supplied standard. A small wax fragment had lodged beneath one support, leaving the unloaded position slightly high. She stopped and asked Zhou to inspect it rather than recording a conveniently neat number. The appointed scale worker cleaned the accepted bearing area and repeated the blank. Yue had noticed a condition she could describe; she had not repaired the scale by touching a piece whose maintenance belonged to someone else's task.

reservoir_ep03_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_007.text: With the blank accepted, Yue weighed the offered comparison sack under the worker's handling rule. Her numbers agreed with the local standard within the posted tolerance. She then copied a deliberately corrected receiving line without erasing its original figure or losing the correction date. Zhou compared both tasks and accepted the appointment. The demonstration's actual hours counted inside today's paid day, leaving time for a limited first copying task. A successful small test had produced a particular job. It had not certified every future grain measurement or opened the reservoir's instrument chamber.

reservoir_ep03_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_008.text: The receiving clerk wrote Yue's lodging and meal authorization to the named houses for the forty-nine-day term. She would sign for actual provision as it occurred. An unused night could not be billed twice, and the granary could not claim that the whole allocation had already been consumed. The final closing account would reconcile actual receipts against the authorized ninety-eight. Yue kept her personal journey remainder separate. She no longer needed to spend tomorrow's grain wages in advance to pay tonight's accepted bed, which changed how much attention she could give the ordinary work.

reservoir_ep03_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_009.text: The stores had begun the recorded interval with one hundred sixty sealed sacks. Twenty-four accepted sacks had arrived, and thirty-two had left under checked dispatches, leaving one hundred fifty-two on the current physical count. Each nominal sack held eight local grain units, but nominal totals would not replace the usable measurement. A damp seam had spoiled part of one sack. Zhou required the rejected amount to be weighed and recorded separately. Yue wrote the sack count first, leaving the usable-grain line open until its actual comparison was complete.

reservoir_ep03_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_010.text: The damaged sack belonged to a particular receiving entry. Its carrier had delivered it with an intact outer tie, and the dampness appeared along a seam not visible under the cover. That observation did not establish who had caused the loss. The store worker isolated it from clean grain and followed the accepted inspection procedure. Yue copied the handling times. Zhou asked the carrier for the available account without threatening to withhold unrelated earned pay. A physical rejection needed a defined receiving action and evidence, rather than a convenient person to blame.

reservoir_ep03_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_011.text: The qualified grain inspector rejected half a local unit from that sack after comparing it with the clean reference. The nominal one thousand two hundred sixteen units therefore gave no more than one thousand two hundred fifteen and a half usable before any other measured loss. Zhou would not round the half back into the store because the number looked untidy. Yue labeled the reference and the inspector's source. The actual accepted grain, its rejected fraction and its nominal package count could all be true while describing different parts of one inventory.

reservoir_ep03_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_012.text: A cooperative member suggested charging the whole sack to the carrier. Zhou asked for the receiving term that made a half-unit rejection into an eight-unit claim. The member could not supply one. The accepted question concerned responsibility for the actual damaged fraction, with its cause still under review. No invented larger loss would create money for other desirable work. Yue saw that precision could protect a carrier without denying the store's real damage. She copied the limited claim for its proper receiver and left the remaining clean grain in its accepted account.

reservoir_ep03_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_013.text: The ordinary store worker moved the isolated sack with a checked trolley. Yue held no overhead load and supplied no strengthening pulse. Her accepted task was the receiving record at the waist-height table. When the trolley's wheel met a raised paving edge, the worker stopped and used the current sound route around it. A faster push would have risked another tear. Yue entered the actual handling delay without calling it wasted time. The task's cost included making it possible for the grain to remain usable after the paper count was correct.

reservoir_ep03_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_014.text: At midday, Zhou checked the day's accepted hours with Yue. The demonstration and first receiving copies had consumed the morning interval. The afternoon would finish three numbered pages, then stop at the posted hour whether or not another arrival looked interesting. She agreed and put the limit on her own sheet. The commission's long calendar existed partly to make these stopping rules possible. It would be easy to explain a late night as dedication and harder to explain the next day's tired copying error to the household whose grain it misassigned.

reservoir_ep03_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_015.text: Jing passed the grain doorway under her own instrument-stock duty and asked whether Yue had received any instruction request. Yue said no; the current appointment concerned ordinary records only. The custodian left a public receiving notice for later questions, without lending sleeves or offering a private lesson after work. The winter-city term still needed closure, and any qualified new exam would need a different fund. Yue appreciated the opportunity's restraint. It preserved a clean beginning for something she hoped to pursue without smuggling it into a job whose members had paid for grain work.

reservoir_ep03_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_016.text: The first three pages included one late receiving mark copied from the previous week. Its date had been changed on the source with the receiver's initials, while a later summary still used the older date. Yue flagged the mismatch without deciding that grain had vanished. Zhou compared the original and dispatch acknowledgment. The carrier had arrived after the desk closed, and physical receipt occurred the following morning. Both times needed their proper labels. A copied date could be wrong without proving a secret theft, and still needed correction before another decision relied on it.

reservoir_ep03_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_017.text: Zhou authorized the specific summary correction and retained the source's visible history. The clerk sent notice to the one account whose statement had used the earlier date. He did not circulate the carrier's private explanation beyond its accepted purpose. Yue prepared the limited copy and checked its receiver. Her practical work produced a different next behavior: the account's storage interval would begin from the actual receiving morning. That consequence mattered more than how impressively she could describe having detected an inconsistency, because it changed an ordinary bill somebody would later pay.

reservoir_ep03_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_018.text: At the end of the posted day, Zhou signed the first accepted equivalent. Yue had earned three copper under the new local order. The receiver paid it after checking the actual interval and gave its wage receipt. Food and lodging stayed with their separate provision accounts. The cash was neither a cultivation reward nor an advance against a future certificate. Yue counted it into the personal purse beside the journey remainder. A fresh livelihood had begun with a modest amount and a record whose cause she could explain without asking anyone to believe in her rank.

reservoir_ep03_019.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_019.text: The evening meal came from the granary's accepted visitor-food order. The cook marked today's real serving and asked Yue whether she expected to use tomorrow's provision at the house or the posted station. She chose the house and agreed to notify any later change before the dispatch cutoff. A prepaid possibility did not mean the cook should prepare two meals and call them both received. Yue liked being asked a small question she could answer. Its clarity made the larger funded term feel like an arrangement among people rather than an invisible favor.

reservoir_ep03_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_020.text: On Day One Thousand Twenty-seven, no grain work was scheduled for Yue. She washed ordinary clothes, rested her shoulder and kept the lodging receiver's current house rules. The commission did not count those acts as another paid day. She could ask for a permitted public room interval, but her winter-city access condition still governed its relevant records. A seventh-stage cultivator might find a blank working day uncomfortable. Yue filled her private page with questions rather than finding an unaccepted household task merely to avoid appearing idle.

reservoir_ep03_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_021.text: Qiu checked the basin's present water-turn roster with its appointed keeper. She offered Yue the public heading and declined the private complaint pages until the proper receiver decided. Yue had expected her ordinary grain appointment to make the request simpler. It made the place and work hours clearer, but did not enlarge another record keeper's consent. The steward wrote the request in the correct book. Yue sat beside the waiting bench and let the difference remain inconvenient. It was better than gaining a confidential page nobody had consciously agreed to show her.

reservoir_ep03_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_022.text: An upstream household's public question concerned flour deliveries, not a demand to reopen the main gate. The writer wanted to know which accepted grain date should appear beside a late water turn. Qiu kept the two questions separate until their respective keepers compared actual times. Yue's grain summary correction could assist that comparison with permission from its source receiver. It would not prove the household's whole account. The first local job had placed her near a real new question, and proximity would require more care rather than fewer boundaries.

reservoir_ep03_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_023.text: That afternoon, the visitor house received a forwarded private envelope for another traveler. Yue's own receiving slot remained empty. She did not take the other person's letter as proof that her own route had failed. The clerk's dispatch list showed different origins and actual departure dates. Yue checked her registered contact and the next expected interval. Her mother could choose what to write and when to answer within the real care circumstances at home. A daughter could keep the route functional without owning the sender's every hour.

reservoir_ep03_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_024.text: Zhou's assistant brought a public copy of the damaged-sack handling procedure to the reading room. Its purpose was to let cooperative members understand the limited rejected fraction and how future receiving checks would work. The paper omitted private accusations that had not been substantiated. Yue read the public version against the original's allowed headings and found one useful simplification: it distinguished package count from usable grain in ordinary language. She asked the assistant to keep that distinction visible even if the half-unit line made the page less elegant than a rounded total.

reservoir_ep03_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_025.text: On Day One Thousand Twenty-eight, Yue went to the public garden behind the house. Its irrigation ditch belonged to the gardener's current accepted turn, and she stepped around the little barrier rather than moving it for a better view. The gardener was pruning ordinary dead stems. He had no need for an apprentice's spiritual diagnosis. Yue asked whether the path was open and received a simple yes. She walked it slowly, glad to be somewhere her most useful decision was about a sound place to put her feet.

reservoir_ep03_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_026.text: From the garden she could see the measuring platform's white stones again. The closure notice remained unchanged. A worker had placed an inspection appointment on the public board, but no result yet followed it. Yue did not interpret the unaltered barrier as institutional neglect. A qualified person needed daylight, sound equipment and an available accepted interval. The water's beauty did not reduce those needs. She turned back before the current visitor limit and kept the upcoming appointment as a date to check, rather than as an inevitable acceptance already achieved.

reservoir_ep03_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_027.text: The private notebook's older small-circuit pages showed why she wanted the next stage. Stable retention had made certain tasks repeatable, but a changing ordinary day still affected the balance she could hold after sleep. She read the observed limits without practicing a new load. Reservoir balance might eventually help a permitted task remain dependable under specified changed conditions. It would not make lost years reappear in her mother's life, settle a household's water rights or turn every ordinary tool into a spiritual extension of her hands.

reservoir_ep03_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_028.text: On Day One Thousand Twenty-nine, the grain house's younger clerk asked Yue whether she preferred the high basin to the winter factory. She said she had not yet worked long enough here to compare their whole practices. He looked disappointed, as if a traveler ought to carry clear opinions ready for every table. Yue asked what he liked about his own work. He showed the new dry shelf he had helped fit above the floor. Its usefulness needed no comparison with another institution to become something he could be proud of.

reservoir_ep03_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_029.text: The shelf held paper, not grain. Its label kept it out of the sack inventory. The clerk had once copied a storage count directly from the room's list of spaces and included two places reserved for empty containers. He told the story without asking Yue to decide whether the error made him foolish. The receiver had corrected the count and changed the form. Yue wrote the lesson privately: a room's capacity was not its present stock. Her own cultivation reservoir required the same distinction, though the two measurements had different units and methods.

reservoir_ep03_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_030.text: A cooperative member arrived with a proposed correction to the damp-sack summary. He wanted it to say that no important loss had occurred. Zhou retained the actual half-unit rejection. The member said the honest fraction might worry buyers who would otherwise trust the whole store. Zhou asked whether an inaccurate public statement would improve that trust after a buyer read the inspection. Yue prepared the version the receiver accepted: a bounded loss, isolated properly, with clean stock separately checked. The public explanation could be understandable without denying what had happened.

reservoir_ep03_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_031.text: The member left grumbling, then returned with an offered cover maker's contact. He had accepted the limited loss and wanted a practical way to prevent another. Zhou took the contact for comparison, not as a contract already signed. Yue was glad the earlier disagreement had not required treating the man as incapable of contributing anything useful. He could prefer a flattering summary and still know an ordinary repair worker whose service might matter. Their next decision would concern an inspected cover and an actual price, rather than the purity of someone's motives.

reservoir_ep03_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_032.text: The visiting room's ordinary wall calendar showed which evenings people could gather without taking a paid hour from the grain work. Yue joined one where a local singer performed a short mountain song under her own offered scope. The singer declined a request for the verse about her absent sister. No audience member bought that memory by bringing tea. Yue listened to the verses actually offered and left the missing one missing. She understood the refusal more keenly after checking a receiving slot that still held no answer from home.

reservoir_ep03_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_033.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty, Yue began her second accepted grain day at the posted hour. Zhou assigned the checked dispatch comparison, not a fresh physical task. The source showed thirty-two sacks leaving through four accepted eight-sack dispatches. One receiving acknowledgment used the packet's prepared date rather than its actual departure date. Yue flagged the distinction before combining it with the store count. The sack total could remain correct while the timing was wrong, and a household's bill might still depend on which timing the summary used.

reservoir_ep03_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_034.text: The downstream receiver confirmed actual arrival from its own original. It had not lost a dispatch and did not want its private worker's illness copied into the public explanation. Zhou accepted the date correction and retained that boundary. Yue prepared a new public line showing the actual departure and receiving days, without assigning a motive to the old copied error. The next storage statement would use those dates. A corrected record could change someone's ordinary cost while preserving a private circumstance that the arithmetic did not need to expose.

reservoir_ep03_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_035.text: At the weighing bench, the scale worker asked Yue to check the copied units on a current form. The margin used an old eight-unit nominal sack label beside a present measured-grain field. Yue proposed separating them clearly and showed the receiver where a reader might confuse the two. Zhou approved the form change for future entries while keeping old forms identifiable. The younger clerk carried the corrected stack to the accepted shelf. He did not burn the earlier pages to make it appear that the house had always measured everything in the clearest possible way.

reservoir_ep03_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_036.text: The water keeper arrived at midday with a public question about grain delivery hours. Zhou could answer when the sacks had actually crossed the grain receiver's table, but he could not certify how long a household had waited at its water station. Yue copied the permitted dispatch summary for the keeper's specific comparison. The private claim pages stayed behind. The connection between their work was becoming real: separate records could meet at a stated question. It would become unreliable if one record began claiming the facts that only the other keeper could measure.

reservoir_ep03_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_037.text: Zhou stopped the ordinary day's copying at the accepted hour. A late visitor wanted his packet included before tomorrow's meeting. The receiver named the next available paid interval and offered the current ordinary emergency route if the deadline genuinely required it. Yue did not stay secretly to make the whole problem disappear. The visitor left his request with its actual receiver. A stopped working day could disappoint someone without proving that the worker lacked resolve. Her second three-copper wage came from completed accepted work, not from how much exhaustion she displayed on leaving.

reservoir_ep03_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_038.text: Jing met her at the meal house with an ordinary spool of thread she had bought herself. One sleeve of her work apron had torn away from the cupboard catch. Yue offered help repairing the cloth after asking whether Jing wanted it. The custodian agreed to the small shared evening task and kept the institutional instrument sleeve entirely out of it. They laughed about a badly placed cupboard hook. Friendship could begin around an owned apron and a consented little repair, without purchasing a private lesson or blurring whose tools would remain in the locked room.

reservoir_ep03_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_039.text: Jing's father had maintained ordinary pumps before she learned sampling. He disliked being introduced as the parent of someone who understood more remarkable things than he did. A pump still needed a sound seal, she said, and her instruments had not made him unnecessary. Yue asked whether he remained at the upper station. Jing said he had retired and chosen a smaller garden, where he wanted visitors to ask about beans rather than old failures. She offered that account for conversation, not as permission for Yue to seek his testimony or repair his life.

reservoir_ep03_040.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_040.text: Qiu sat with them only after finishing her accepted evening round. She brought her own mending and no operating original. The steward described the first winter she had mistaken a household's polite silence for agreement with a changed turn. The household had waited because its representative did not know how to object at the desk. The error required a real revised schedule and an apology delivered to its own receiver. Yue listened without translating the story into proof that Qiu would always be wrong or could now do no wrong after acknowledging it.

reservoir_ep03_041.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_041.text: The steward's lesson did not make every silent household a hidden opponent. Some genuinely accepted a turn; some wished to decline public discussion; some simply had another task underway. Qiu now asked what agreement had actually been offered and by whom. Yue thought of Fu's proposed sibling work swap, left unaccepted at their first meeting. An absent person's silence could not answer it. The quiet evening had become useful because its stories described particular changes in practice, rather than giving Yue a universal rule to impose on the next person who spoke softly.

reservoir_ep03_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_042.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-one, the lower-house receiver acknowledged the forwarded household request. The meeting would compare work and water calendars during the coming period, with each participant's own consent. The acknowledgment named no final turn change. Qiu posted the public date and kept private contacts inside their covered file. Yue's winter-city access condition would determine which comparative records she could request there. Her travel route would determine which earlier offered conversation she could accurately refer to. The new meeting would begin with those actual differences instead of erasing them for convenience.

reservoir_ep03_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_043.text: The younger grain clerk wanted to attend but had an overlapping paid shift. Zhou asked whether a qualified coworker wished to trade the particular interval. One did, under the same total accepted hours and wage rate, and both signed the exchange. Yue copied the new assignment after the receiver accepted it. The old interval did not become an additional paid day, and the coworker gained no permanent duty to cover every future public meeting. A modest real calendar change had made this attendance possible without requiring anyone's generosity to remain endlessly available.

reservoir_ep03_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_044.text: Yue had no grain shift on the meeting's preparatory day, but she would still need a clear accepted role before handling another household's private pages. Qiu offered the public agenda for reading and said its receiver would decide further access. Yue read it at the table, then returned it. She could prepare questions from permitted information without privately gathering a duplicate archive. The paper's return felt less like losing knowledge when she wrote down the source address. A useful question could travel with a way to request its evidence again.

reservoir_ep03_045.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_045.text: The evening sky cleared enough to show the basin's reflected stars. From the public veranda, the reflections trembled whenever the ordinary feeder stirred. Yue did not treat the number of visible stars as a reservoir measurement. She watched until the house's accepted quiet hour, then walked back by the sound route. The scene had no result to certify and no secret technique to discover. Its pleasure remained real. After a day among figures and missing permissions, she was grateful for an ordinary experience that could matter without becoming evidence for a larger claim.

reservoir_ep03_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_046.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-two, the grain receiver accepted the cover maker's inspection appointment. She examined the isolated damaged seam and the current storage conditions before quoting a repair. Yue had not been scheduled to copy the work and watched only its public offered portion. The maker found a worn seam and an inadequate cover fit that could admit spray under certain carriage conditions. She did not claim to reconstruct the whole road journey from cloth alone. Her report supplied a practical condition to correct and left the cause review within its evidence.

reservoir_ep03_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_047.text: Zhou authorized one fitted replacement from the ordinary materials allocation after comparing its price and scope. The half-unit already lost did not return when the seam was repaired. The clean remainder stayed in its accepted container. Yue copied the public notice during her next actual work interval rather than starting a free unrecorded task today. The difference between fixing future conditions and undoing past harm seemed obvious on the grain scale. She wanted to remember it when a future cultivation result made a less ordinary kind of hope tempting.

reservoir_ep03_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_048.text: A mother at the visitor house asked whether a successful reservoir cultivator could recover years lost to difficult work. Yue said her own practice had given no such power. The woman had heard a traveling account about a higher realm and was asking a real question, not inviting ridicule. Yue named the ordinary clinician's receiving contact for the current pain concern and distinguished it from the impossible promise she could not make. The woman took the contact. Respect did not require keeping a comforting claim alive when nobody present could honestly support it.

reservoir_ep03_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_049.text: That afternoon, Yue's private receiving slot held an ordinary forwarding acknowledgment again. It confirmed that the family route remained current. She would receive any actual letter through the basin's named contact during the term, subject to documented interruptions. The clerk offered no interpretation of the silence. Yue thanked him and left without asking him to guess what her mother might be feeling. Other people's careful work could carry a message when one existed. It could not relieve her uncertainty by inventing a message that had not arrived.

reservoir_ep03_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_050.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-three, Qiu reviewed the visitor provision account. Six actual nights and the corresponding meals had been accepted so far within the forty-nine-day grain term. The remainder stayed authorized and unconsumed. Yue had not billed the house for the personal journey's earlier nights. The meal receiver corrected one duplicated room number before it became a second serving claim. No dramatic fraud had been uncovered; an ordinary copying mistake had been stopped. Keeping the accounts accurate required such small interventions even when everyone's intentions were cooperative.

reservoir_ep03_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_051.text: The paid lodging order covered an actual visitor room, not unlimited guests. Yue could invite Jing for a permitted conversation during the house's public hours, but another person's overnight stay would require its own acceptance. Jing preferred the ordinary mending table downstairs. They sat there while the grain clerk finished his private letter. Each person kept the offered conversation's limits without making the room cold. Yue was learning that clear property and time boundaries could make companionship easier, because nobody had to guess which kindness might later be treated as a permanent duty.

reservoir_ep03_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_052.text: Qiu's present water reading stood lower than the previous evening's. The appointed keeper explained the accepted downstream turn and the checked feeder variation within his own record. He made no claim about next month's rain. Yue listened from the public station and copied only the permitted summary. A forecast might help plan a bounded comparison, but it would not enter stored water as if the forecast had already fallen into the basin. The distinction between hoped quantity and actual usable quantity would matter again when she finally tested her own reservoir.

reservoir_ep03_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_053.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-four, wind struck the grain house while the younger clerk was carrying an empty wicker basket through the yard. A shutter broke loose from its worn catch and hit the basket's rim. The basket leaped out of his hands. Yue caught his sleeve at waist height and pulled him back onto the sound paving as the shutter swung again. He shouted more from surprise than pain. The nearest store worker shut the inner door, and Zhou called the yard clear.

reservoir_ep03_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_054.text: The clerk's name was Tian Yu. He stood blinking beside Yue, then began laughing at the ridiculous basket lying upside down in a puddle. The laugh stopped when another gust slammed the shutter against the wall. Yue released his sleeve once he had his footing. Her shoulder had taken an ordinary brief pull, so she told Zhou what had happened and kept away from further handling. Tian retrieved nothing until the carpenter secured the loose panel. They watched the basket float slowly toward the drain like an incompetent little boat.

reservoir_ep03_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_055.text: Zhou sent Yue to the sheltered bench and asked the house's clinician to check ordinary movement. The examination found no fresh injury, and her shoulder's existing limit remained in place. The clinician recommended rest from pulling that afternoon. Yue obeyed without having to prove that the incident had been harmless. Tian brought her tea with both hands, embarrassed by how much it shook. She said the basket had probably traveled farther without him than it ever had at work. He laughed properly then, and the noise loosened something tight in her chest.

reservoir_ep03_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_056.text: The carpenter found that the shutter catch had worn through beside its last sound inspection mark. He replaced the actual failed piece and accepted the secured panel after checking its movement in the current wind. Zhou kept the yard closed while the work was underway. Inside, the grain remained dry behind its inner barrier. Tian mourned the basket until the gardener recovered it at the sound drain mouth. Its rim needed repair, but its astonishing voyage became the meal house's best story that evening.

reservoir_ep03_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_057.text: Yue listened to Tian tell it three times, each with a larger wave. On the third telling he claimed the basket had almost reached the reservoir. Zhou raised an eyebrow, and Tian admitted that the gardener's shoe had stopped it after six ordinary paces. Nobody demanded that a supper joke become an inspection report. Yue liked him more for laughing at his own exaggeration. The exact handling record rested safely in the store, while the room could enjoy a story whose listeners understood where its playful part began.

reservoir_ep03_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_058.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-five, Yue completed the third accepted grain day. Her ordinary baseline was comfortable after the previous afternoon's rest. Zhou assigned the final current-stock comparison and its limited public explanation, with no lifting. The physical tally confirmed one hundred fifty-two nominal sacks, the isolated half-unit rejection and no additional usable loss from the shutter incident. Tian brought the source pages to the waist-height table with a carefully repaired basket. Its new rim made a small crooked arc he intended to keep rather than trim smooth.

reservoir_ep03_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_059.text: A member challenged the public date correction during the afternoon receiving interval. He had paid storage against the copied earlier date and wanted the difference returned. Zhou compared the actual accepted morning, the old bill and the member's receipt. The correction did affect one priced day. He authorized the real refund from the storage receiver's own account, rather than from Yue's wages or the provision order. The member counted the coin, grew quieter and asked Tian whether the basket story was true. Tian supplied the six-pace version without disappointment.

reservoir_ep03_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_060.text: At closing, Zhou paid Yue another three copper. Across her first three accepted day equivalents she had earned nine. The visitor provision record showed actual food and nights, with the remainder still available through the written term. Yue put the wage receipt away and joined Tian outside, where the wind had settled. He wanted to show her a bright weed flowering between two stones. Its color looked improbable beside the brown grain-house wall. She crouched on sound paving and admired it without needing it to cure anyone or carry a message.

reservoir_ep03_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_061.text: Qiu found them there and asked whether the basin's next calendar meeting could use the public grain-date correction. Zhou had already permitted the relevant extract, and its source address was clear. Yue would bring that limited fact if the receiver accepted her actual role. Tian asked if he could attend under his traded interval. Qiu checked the posted appointment and confirmed the new time. For once, the questions ended in a straightforward yes. They stood together until the little flower's color faded with the ordinary evening light.

reservoir_ep03_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_062.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-six, Yue's first real family letter reached the named basin contact. Her mother described a day spent sorting small things at home, with the heavier task left to the person actually helping her. She complained about a neighbor's overstrong tea and asked whether the plateau wind had stolen Yue's hat. The words made Yue laugh before they made her cry. There was pain and limitation in the account, but also a person choosing what to say. Lost years remained lost; this particular morning at home had nonetheless belonged to her mother.

reservoir_ep03_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_063.text: Yue answered the hat question first. She then asked about the next ordinary care appointment and whether a later visit would be welcome during the family's actual available days. She did not promise a date before comparing the grain term and her mother's preference. The letter lay open beside Tian's repaired basket, and its small familiar jokes made the room feel less distant. When Jing arrived for their agreed mending evening, Yue offered the tea complaint rather than the private care details. Jing laughed and admitted she liked tea almost strong enough to chew.

reservoir_ep03_064.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_064.text: On Day One Thousand Thirty-seven, Fu Lian's current receiving message confirmed that she would attend the calendar comparison under her own agreed work arrangement. She wanted the meeting to settle a usable question, because her brother's next grain shift and the household's water turn would collide again soon. Yue read the dates beside Zhou's actual dispatch correction and her selected journey's sources. This time the mismatch had a face she knew. She put the permitted packet near tomorrow's appointment and wondered which person's inconvenience the room would be tempted to overlook first.

reservoir_ep03_065.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep03_065.text: Outside, the repaired shutter held against a fresh gust. Yue tied tomorrow's packet with ordinary thread, then folded her mother's letter separately. The basket waited upside down, finally dry and still.
